-   Oklahoma stumbled into another botched execution (John Marion Grant).

mediaItem.itemTitle: Jason Flom and Kim Kardashian on Julius Jones - UPDATE
mediaItem.summaryNotes: This episode of Wrongful Conviction with Jason Flom focuses on the case of Julius Jones, who was on death row in Oklahoma for the murder of Paul Howell in 1999.  Despite strong evidence pointing to his innocence, including sworn affidavits from multiple individuals stating that Chris Jordan, the co-defendant, confessed to being the shooter and framing Jones, Julius was convicted largely due to incentivized testimony and ineffective defense counsel.  The podcast features Kim Kardashian, Julius's attorney Dale Beish, and his mother and sister, highlighting the flawed trial, racial bias, and systemic issues within the justice system.  It details the exculpatory evidence, including the lack of Julius's DNA on key evidence and the fact that the eyewitness description better matched Chris Jordan.  While Governor Stitt granted clemency, commuting his sentence to life without parole, the fight for Julius Jones's complete freedom continues, with advocates urging public action and highlighting the broader issue of wrongful convictions.

featuredIndividual.convictionYear: Not explicitly stated in the transcript, but implied to be shortly after the 1999 crime, given he's been on death row for over 20 years.
featuredIndividual.sentence: Originally sentenced to death. Commuted to life without the possibility of parole.
featuredIndividual.timeServed: Over 20 years (as of the podcast recording).
contributingFactorsRaw: Planted evidence (gun hidden in Jones's home by Chris Jordan).
Eyewitness misidentification (description matched Chris Jordan more closely, but witness ID not fully explored).
Ineffective defense counsel (failure to present alibi, investigate witnesses, or challenge inconsistencies in prosecution's case).
Racial bias (juror's racist comment, statistical evidence of racial disparity in death penalty cases in Oklahoma).
featuredIndividual.status: Sentence commuted to life without parole, but advocates continue to fight for full exoneration.
organizationsInvolvedRaw: Not explicitly named in transcript, but implied involvement of legal teams, advocacy groups, and individuals like Kim Kardashian, Scott Budnick, Reverend C.C. Jones Davis.
innocenceLawyersRaw: Dale Beish, assistant federal public defender, involved in clemency proceedings since 2016.
featuredIndividual.narrativeOriginalCrime: Paul Howell was shot and killed in his driveway in Edmond, Oklahoma, during a robbery for his GMC Suburban on July 28, 1999.
keyEvidenceProsecutionRaw: Testimony of co-defendant Chris Jordan blaming Julius Jones.
Testimony of confidential informant Liddell King.
Gun found in Julius Jones's parents' home.
Megan Tobey's (victim's sister) eyewitness identification (though description was ambiguous and arguably matched Jordan more).
featuredIndividual.trialDefenderNotes: Defense rested without presenting any evidence or witnesses. Failed to challenge inconsistencies in Chris Jordan's statements, alibi for Julius, or present evidence of Jordan's confessions to others.
keyEvidenceExonerationRaw: Sworn affidavits from multiple individuals (Manuel Little John, Christopher Berry, Roderick Wesley) stating Chris Jordan confessed to the crime and framing Julius Jones.
Inconsistencies in Chris Jordan's statements to police.
Eyewitness description fitting Chris Jordan more than Julius Jones (hair length).
Julius Jones's alibi (being home with family).
Lack of Julius Jones's saliva DNA on the bandana (though trace DNA found, potentially from transfer).
featuredIndividual.actualPerpetratorDetails: Chris Jordan is heavily implicated by his own inconsistent statements, confessions to multiple individuals, and the eyewitness description matching him more closely. He received a deal for his testimony against Julius Jones.

keyQuotesRaw: Kim Kardashian: "What if that was my son? What would I do if my son got set up like this? So we got to fight for this guy. We got to help him get his life back."

Dale Beish: "This case got the attention it deserved when Viola Davis and Julius Tennen produced the last offense. That put light on this injustice and wrongful conviction. What's troubling to me and we should all be concerned about this is that without the last offense, no one would be interested in this case. Julius would have been just another African-American man in prison saying he was innocent. One of the 4% and no one would care."
Antoinette Jones: "My brother Julius...He did not kill Paul Howe. My brother is a human being. He is not a number...He never got a fair defense...He never got a juror of his peers."
Madeline Jones: "Justice is growing because it wants to be heard and it wants to be fulfilled, what it's really meant to be justice for all, not just for some of us."
Jason Flom (Juror quote): "Why are we wasting our time here? We ought to just take that N out back and bury him outside the jail."
systemicIssuesRaw: Racial bias in the criminal justice system and death penalty.
Tunnel vision in police investigations, focusing on a suspect and ignoring contradictory evidence.
Difficulty in overturning wrongful convictions even with compelling evidence of innocence.
policyRecommendationsRaw: Call the governor's office and elected officials to advocate for Julius Jones.
Stay informed and engaged in criminal justice reform.
Support organizations working on wrongful conviction cases.
personalNarrativeRaw: Julius Jones: Despite being on death row for over 20 years for a crime he maintains he didn't commit, he displays grace and inspires others with his resilience.

Family: The Jones family has experienced a "20 plus year shock" and "American nightmare." They express devastation at the injustice and are tirelessly advocating for Julius's freedom and highlighting his good character.
additionalResourcesRaw: Documentary "The Last Defense" with Viola Davis.
